nodes.label: Arrhythmias on abrupt beta-blocker withdrawal
nodes.rationale: Long-term beta blockade up-regulates beta receptors; sudden stop worsens angina or hypertension, so taper over at least a few weeks.

nodes.label: Beta-blockers
nodes.rationale: Do not cause postural hypotension because alpha adrenoceptors remain functional. Names end in -olol except labetalol and carvedilol. | Must not be stopped abruptly; taper over 2 to 3 weeks to avoid rebound angina, MI, and hypertension. | Not first-line for hypertension; abrupt stop risks angina, MI, death so taper over weeks.

nodes.label: Beta-blocker withdrawal syndrome
nodes.rationale: Abrupt withdrawal can cause severe hypertension, angina, MI and sudden death in ischemic heart disease; taper over a few weeks.

nodes.label: Cardioselective beta-blockers
nodes.rationale: Block beta-1 at doses 50-100 fold lower than beta-2; selectivity lost at high doses; fewer effects on lung, peripheral resistance and carbohydrate metabolism. | Block only beta1, so they do not worsen asthma

nodes.label: Esmolol
nodes.rationale: Hydrolyzed rapidly by red blood cell esterase, half-life 9-10 minutes; IV only.

nodes.label: Intrinsic sympathomimetic activity
nodes.rationale: Partial agonists stimulate the receptor weakly while blocking more potent catecholamines, giving a diminished reduction of cardiac rate and output.

nodes.label: Masked hypoglycemia
nodes.rationale: Beta blockade decreases glycogenolysis and glucagon and blunts tremor/tachycardia warning signs; diaphoresis persists (cholinergic).

nodes.label: Pindolol
nodes.rationale: Has intrinsic sympathomimetic activity (ISA); avoid in angina and after MI.

nodes.label: Propranolol
nodes.rationale: Prototype nonselective beta-blocker; about 25% oral bioavailability due to first-pass effect; lipophilic, crosses the blood-brain barrier (useful in migraine prophylaxis, more CNS adverse effects). | Lippincott lists athletes and physically active patients as a possible contraindication to beta-blockers (Fig. 16.9); reasons are applied from propranolol's own effects.

nodes.label: Abrupt drug withdrawal syndrome
nodes.rationale: Sudden withdrawal of benzodiazepines and antiepileptic agents can cause withdrawal syndrome.

nodes.label: Absence seizures
nodes.rationale: Brief loss of consciousness, onset age 3 to 5, three-per-second spike and wave on EEG. | Begin at age 4 to 12 years; EEG shows generalized 3-Hz waves.

nodes.label: Antiepileptic drugs
nodes.rationale: Suppress seizures but do not cure or prevent epilepsy.

nodes.label: Antiepileptic monotherapy
nodes.rationale: Better adherence and fewer side effects than combination therapy; never more than three AEDs at a time.

nodes.label: Epilepsy
nodes.rationale: Sudden, excessive, synchronous discharge of cerebral neurons; seizures controlled with one drug in about 75% of patients.

nodes.label: Ethosuximide
nodes.rationale: Abrupt discontinuation may cause seizures; periodic CBCs because blood dyscrasias can occur.

nodes.label: Pregabalin
nodes.rationale: Over 90% renally eliminated, so dose must be adjusted in renal dysfunction.

nodes.label: Tiagabine
nodes.rationale: Seizures occurred in patients without epilepsy, so it should not be used for other indications.

nodes.label: Bleomycin
nodes.rationale: Toxicity in lung and skin because bleomycin-inactivating hydrolase is low in lung and absent in skin.

nodes.label: Acetazolamide
nodes.rationale: Avoided in hepatic cirrhosis because it decreases NH4+ excretion.

nodes.label: Halothane
nodes.rationale: Needs precise concentration control and arterial gas monitoring because it depresses myocardium and respiratory centers. | Inhibits uterine contraction so not used for vaginal delivery.

nodes.label: Halothane hepatitis
nodes.rationale: Trifluoroacetic acid metabolite causes hepatic necrosis, about 1 in 10,000 patients.

nodes.label: Mannitol
nodes.rationale: Not absorbed orally; given intravenously.

nodes.label: Proximal convoluted tubule
nodes.rationale: Reabsorbs about 65% of filtered Na+, yet diuretics acting here are weak because the loop of Henle downstream reabsorbs the extra load.

nodes.label: Child dose formulas (Young's, Dilling's, body surface area)

nodes.label: Chloramphenicol
nodes.rationale: Neonates have low glucuronidation capacity and immature renal function

nodes.label: Alcohol withdrawal
nodes.rationale: Benzodiazepines work through cross-tolerance with alcohol.

nodes.label: Anterograde amnesia
nodes.rationale: Important treatment information should be repeated after the drug wears off.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepines
nodes.rationale: Safer than barbiturates because lethal dose is over 1000-fold the therapeutic dose; addictive potential limits use to short periods | Short-acting agents preferred for preanesthetic anxiety and insomnia as they cause no hangover; long-acting better for anxiety, withdrawal, seizures. | Oral clefts in early pregnancy; avoided in labor because of neonatal hypotonia and altered thermoregulation.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepine adverse effects
nodes.rationale: Drowsiness, ataxia, cognitive impairment; respiratory depression exaggerated in sleep apnea and COPD; overdose seldom lethal unless alcohol or opioids taken.

nodes.label: Benzodiazepine withdrawal and dependence
nodes.rationale: Short half-life drugs such as triazolam give more abrupt, severe withdrawal; taper gradually or substitute long-acting diazepam or chlordiazepoxide.

nodes.label: Flumazenil
nodes.rationale: May precipitate withdrawal in dependent patients or seizures in mixed overdose with tricyclics; short half-life needs repeat dosing.

nodes.label: Flurazepam
nodes.rationale: Rarely used because extended half-life causes daytime sedation and accumulation, especially in the elderly.

nodes.label: General anesthetic mechanism: GABA-A potentiation
nodes.rationale: No single receptor identified; chemically unrelated compounds cause unconsciousness.

nodes.label: Increased frequency of GABA chloride channel opening
nodes.norm_label: increased frequency of gaba chloride channel opening

nodes.label: Lorazepam
nodes.rationale: Anxiolytic benzodiazepines are drugs of choice for anxiety and agitation of amphetamine or cocaine abuse; trazodone and hydroxyzine are inferior for rapid anxiolysis.

nodes.label: Nonbenzodiazepine hypnotics (Z-drugs)
nodes.rationale: Bind the benzodiazepine site, reversed by flumazenil; do not significantly alter sleep stages; less tolerance, dependence and rebound insomnia.

nodes.label: Status epilepticus
nodes.rationale: Life threatening, so it needs emergency parenteral treatment with a fast-acting drug followed by a slow-acting one.

nodes.label: Withdrawal seizures from abrupt AED cessation
nodes.norm_label: withdrawal seizures from abrupt aed cessation
nodes.rationale: Taper over 3 to 6 months or more; benzodiazepines and barbiturates especially need very gradual withdrawal.

nodes.label: Zaleplon
nodes.rationale: Rapid elimination (half-life about 1 hour) gives fewer residual psychomotor and cognitive effects.

nodes.label: Zolpidem
nodes.rationale: Rifampin shortens its half-life; CYP3A4 inhibitors lengthen it. Complex sleep behaviors reported.

nodes.label: Nandrolone
nodes.rationale: The book does not name nandrolone; its androgen section applies. Several points tagged [not in book].

nodes.label: Virilization and premature epiphyseal closure
nodes.rationale: Androgens cause virilization of a female fetus and premature closing of epiphyseal plates in children.

nodes.label: Chelation
nodes.rationale: Di- or trivalent cations (Ca2+ in dairy) bind tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones and iron, making them harder to absorb.

nodes.label: Plasma protein binding displacement
nodes.rationale: Usually not clinically relevant because clearance rises, but matters for drugs with a low therapeutic margin.

nodes.label: Reduced fluoroquinolone absorption with divalent cations
nodes.norm_label: reduced fluoroquinolone absorption with divalent cations
nodes.rationale: Sucralfate, aluminum or magnesium antacids, iron or zinc supplements and calcium reduce fluoroquinolone absorption.

nodes.label: Reduced gastric acid secretion and increased mucus and bicarbonate
nodes.norm_label: reduced gastric acid secretion and increased mucus and bicarbonate

nodes.label: Sucralfate
nodes.rationale: Binds proteins, so contraindicated with enteral feeding.

nodes.label: Local anesthetics
nodes.rationale: Weak bases given as hydrochloride salts; the nonionized base diffuses into the nerve membrane; lipophilicity relates to potency.

nodes.label: Scopolamine
nodes.rationale: Greater CNS action and longer duration than atropine; blocks short-term memory; sedating; abuse potential; works better prophylactically.

nodes.label: Antiseizure monotherapy
nodes.rationale: Fewer adverse effects, no antiepileptic drug interactions, lower cost, better compliance.

nodes.label: Focal seizures with impaired awareness
nodes.rationale: Impaired consciousness puts the patient at risk of injury, so treatment is justified; automatisms are common.

nodes.label: Ion trapping
nodes.rationale: Alkalinizing urine ionizes weak acids and cuts back-diffusion; acidifying urine does so for weak bases.

nodes.label: Levetiracetam
nodes.rationale: Does not affect the pharmacokinetics of other antiepileptic drugs and is not significantly altered by them. | Renally cleared with few interactions, suiting elderly patients with comorbidities.

nodes.label: Renal drug elimination
nodes.rationale: Glomerular filtration, active tubular secretion and passive tubular reabsorption.

nodes.label: Urinary alkalinization
nodes.rationale: Sodium bicarbonate raises the nonionized fraction of amphetamine, enhancing renal tubular reabsorption.

nodes.label: Direct action on colonic nerve fibers
nodes.norm_label: direct action on colonic nerve fibers

nodes.label: Mycoses
nodes.rationale: Fungi are eukaryotes with chitin cell walls and ergosterol membranes, grow slowly, so few drugs target cell division.

nodes.label: Nystatin
nodes.rationale: Not given parenterally because of systemic toxicity; negligible GI absorption.

nodes.label: Undecylenic acid
nodes.rationale: Fungistatic, fungicidal at higher concentration; less effective than imidazoles and tolnaftate.

nodes.label: Cocaine
nodes.rationale: Blocks the Na+/Cl- dependent norepinephrine transporter, so norepinephrine accumulates and small catecholamine doses have magnified effects. | Only natural local anesthetic; not used clinically because of adverse effects and abuse potential.

nodes.label: Ester local anesthetics
nodes.rationale: Metabolized by plasma butyrylcholinesterase, so levels are higher in patients with decreased or atypical cholinesterase.

nodes.label: Gemfibrozil
nodes.rationale: Inhibits hepatic metabolism of repaglinide, markedly increasing its effect; concurrent use contraindicated.

nodes.label: HMG CoA reductase inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Marked hepatic first-pass extraction so dominant effect is on the liver. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia lacks LDL receptors so benefit is much less.

nodes.label: Pravastatin
nodes.rationale: Only statin not metabolized by CYP450.

nodes.label: Rhabdomyolysis
nodes.rationale: Risk is higher with renal insufficiency, vitamin D deficiency, hypothyroidism, advanced age, female sex, or drugs such as azole antifungals, protease inhibitors, cyclosporine, erythromycin, gemfibrozil, niacin.

nodes.label: Statins
nodes.rationale: Contraindicated in pregnancy, lactation and active liver disease; hepatic insufficiency can cause drug accumulation.

nodes.label: Migraine
nodes.rationale: Pain may be due to extracranial and intracranial arterial vasodilation releasing substance P, neurokinin A and CGRP.

nodes.rationale: High HBV resistance with long therapy, so no longer recommended in hepatitis B guidelines.

nodes.label: Antiemetic effect of antipsychotics
nodes.rationale: Mediated by D2 blockade in the chemoreceptor trigger zone of the medulla.

nodes.label: Extrapyramidal symptoms
nodes.rationale: Dopamine blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway leaves a relative excess of cholinergic influence; dystonia in hours to days, akathisia in days to weeks, parkinsonism in weeks to months.

nodes.label: Tardive dyskinesia
nodes.rationale: Postulated to result from extra dopamine receptors synthesized after long-term blockade, making the neuron supersensitive; may be irreversible; anti-EPS drugs may worsen it.

nodes.label: Block epithelial sodium transport in distal tubule
nodes.norm_label: block epithelial sodium transport in distal tubule

nodes.label: Epithelial sodium channel blockade
nodes.rationale: Effect does not depend on aldosterone being present.

nodes.label: Eplerenone
nodes.rationale: More selective for aldosterone receptors; less gynecomastia; metabolized by CYP3A4. | Specific for the mineralocorticoid receptor, so avoids the gynecomastia of spironolactone.

nodes.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
nodes.norm_label: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

nodes.label: Potassium-sparing diuretics
nodes.rationale: Avoided in severe renal dysfunction because of hyperkalemia risk; potassium must be monitored.

nodes.label: Spironolactone
nodes.rationale: Also binds progesterone and androgen receptors, causing gynecomastia.

nodes.label: Atropinization in organophosphate poisoning
nodes.rationale: Endpoint is adequate oxygenation and dried pulmonary secretions, not tachycardia or mydriasis; doses are doubled (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 mg).

nodes.label: Dose-dependent cardiac effect of atropine
nodes.rationale: Low dose blocks presynaptic M1 receptors and slightly slows the heart; higher doses block M2 receptors on the SA node and raise heart rate.

nodes.label: Pilocarpine
nodes.rationale: Tertiary amine, uncharged, enters CNS; drug of choice for emergency lowering of intraocular pressure. | Drug of choice for emergency lowering of intraocular pressure in acute glaucoma attack.

nodes.label: Reserpine
nodes.rationale: Seldom used now: newer agents have better adverse-effect profiles and fewer interactions; effects persist days to weeks because vesicular transporter must be replenished

nodes.label: Half-life three times that of epoetin alfa
nodes.norm_label: half-life three times that of epoetin alfa

nodes.label: Anesthetics
nodes.rationale: No single agent gives all objectives (sedation, amnesia, muscle relaxation, reflex suppression, analgesia), so several drug categories are combined.

nodes.label: Induction, maintenance and recovery of general anesthesia
nodes.norm_label: induction, maintenance and recovery of general anesthesia

nodes.label: Inhalational anesthetics
nodes.rationale: Steep dose-response curves, narrow therapeutic index and no antagonists.

nodes.label: Minimum alveolar concentration
nodes.rationale: Inverse of MAC is an index of potency; more lipid soluble means lower MAC and higher potency.

nodes.label: Propofol
nodes.rationale: Short hypnosis after IV bolus is due to redistribution from the CNS to muscle and fat. | Replaced thiopental as first choice for induction; supplied as soybean oil and egg phospholipid emulsion because poorly water soluble.

nodes.label: Redistribution of intravenous anesthetics
nodes.rationale: Rapid recovery after a single bolus is due to redistribution; fat reservoir delays recovery after repeat doses or infusions.

nodes.label: Reduced cardiac output
nodes.rationale: More cardiac output goes to the brain, so intravenous anesthetic dose must be reduced and titrated slowly.

nodes.label: Alpha-1 receptors
nodes.rationale: Gq-coupled: phospholipase C gives IP3 and DAG, IP3 releases Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum.

nodes.label: Beta-1 receptors
nodes.rationale: Heart contains predominantly beta-1 receptors; activation raises cAMP.

nodes.label: Beta-2 receptors
nodes.rationale: Higher affinity for epinephrine than norepinephrine; skeletal muscle vasculature is responsive to circulating epinephrine.

nodes.label: Catecholamines
nodes.rationale: 3,4-dihydroxybenzene group; high potency, rapid inactivation by COMT and MAO (brief action parenterally, inactive orally), poor CNS penetration because polar.

nodes.label: Dopamine
nodes.rationale: Low dose stimulates beta-1; very high dose alpha-1 vasoconstriction; D1/D2 receptors dilate renal and mesenteric vessels. Renal-dose dopamine has limited clinical utility.

nodes.label: Epinephrine
nodes.rationale: Low doses: beta effects (vasodilation) predominate; high doses: alpha effects (vasoconstriction) strongest. Adrenal medulla releases about 80% epinephrine and 20% norepinephrine.

nodes.label: Isoproterenol
nodes.rationale: Nonselective beta-1/beta-2 agonist, so rarely used therapeutically.

nodes.label: Norepinephrine
nodes.rationale: Greater vasoconstriction than epinephrine because it does not cause compensatory beta-2 vasodilation; weak beta-2 activity explains why it is not useful in bronchospasm or anaphylaxis.

nodes.label: Norepinephrine synthesis
nodes.rationale: Tyrosine to DOPA to dopamine to norepinephrine; hydroxylation of tyrosine is the rate-limiting step.

nodes.label: Terbutaline
nodes.rationale: Injectable form used off-label as uterine relaxant in premature labor, not beyond 72 hours.

nodes.label: Therapeutic drug monitoring of immunosuppressants
nodes.rationale: Narrow therapeutic index and large inter-individual variability in blood concentrations

nodes.label: Sodium thiosulfate
nodes.rationale: Weak fungistatic agent, safe in pregnancy.

nodes.label: Leucovorin
nodes.rationale: N5-formyl form of tetrahydrofolate; rescues normal cells from methotrexate toxicity.

nodes.label: Megaloblastic anemia
nodes.rationale: Folic acid alone reverses the blood abnormality and masks vitamin B12 deficiency, which can progress to severe neurologic disease, so give folic acid with vitamin B12.

nodes.label: Efavirenz
nodes.rationale: Safe in patients co-infected with tuberculosis because of lower potential for interactions with rifamycins.

nodes.label: NACO first-line HIV regimen
nodes.rationale: Start ART only after active opportunistic infections are treated or stabilised; treat TB first then start ART. Monotherapy, dual therapy, unboosted PIs and treatment interruptions are never used.

nodes.label: Non-competitive allosteric inhibition of reverse transcriptase
nodes.norm_label: non-competitive allosteric inhibition of reverse transcriptase

nodes.label: Adverse drug reaction
nodes.rationale: WHO definition: noxious, unpleasant, unintended response at normal doses; excludes therapeutic failure, overdose, abuse, noncompliance and medication errors.

nodes.label: Drug response in the elderly
nodes.rationale: Increased sensitivity to CNS depressants and anticoagulants, reduced physiological reserve, so doses are generally reduced.

nodes.label: Error-prone abbreviations
nodes.rationale: Q1d mistaken for QID gives four times the dose; handwritten U read as 0 or 4, so write Unit.

nodes.label: Polypharmacy
nodes.rationale: More drugs prescribed means more adverse effects and more medication errors; largest risk factor for medication error. | Hard to remember different dosing intervals; prescriptions should be reviewed regularly.

nodes.label: Prescribing cascade
nodes.rationale: An adverse effect is misread as a new disorder and treated with another drug, adding further adverse effects and interactions. | An ADR is mistaken for a new condition and treated with another drug, which adds new ADRs.

nodes.label: Acetylcholine
nodes.rationale: Quaternary ammonium compound; therapeutically unimportant because of diffuse actions and rapid inactivation by cholinesterases.

nodes.label: Carbachol
nodes.rationale: Muscarinic and nicotinic actions; rarely used because of high potency, nonselectivity and long duration.

nodes.label: Direct-acting cholinergic agonists
nodes.rationale: Choline esters (ACh, carbachol, bethanechol) and alkaloids (nicotine, pilocarpine); little specificity limits clinical usefulness.

nodes.label: Hemicholinium
nodes.rationale: Choline uptake is the rate-limiting step in ACh synthesis.

nodes.label: Neurotransmitters
nodes.rationale: Hydrophilic, so they act on cell-surface membrane receptors; release is triggered by action potential and raised intracellular Ca2+.

nodes.label: Cidofovir
nodes.rationale: Probenecid and IV saline are coadministered to reduce nephrotoxicity; slow elimination of active metabolite allows prolonged dosing intervals.

nodes.label: Foscarnet
nodes.rationale: Does not need activation by viral or cellular kinases; chelates divalent cations causing hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia.

nodes.label: Trifluridine
nodes.rationale: Too toxic for systemic use because the triphosphate also incorporates into cellular DNA; restricted to topical ophthalmic use.

nodes.label: Viral DNA and RNA polymerase inhibition
nodes.norm_label: viral dna and rna polymerase inhibition

nodes.label: Seizures and arrhythmias in theophylline overdose
nodes.norm_label: seizures and arrhythmias in theophylline overdose

nodes.label: Types of drug action (activation, inhibition, complexation, neutralization)
nodes.norm_label: types of drug action (activation, inhibition, complexation, neutralization)

nodes.label: Amitriptyline
nodes.rationale: Potent antimuscarinic activity raises intraocular pressure; alpha-1 antagonism gives high orthostasis and fall risk in the elderly.

nodes.label: Antimuscarinic contraindications and cautions
nodes.rationale: Parasympathetic depression can unmask sympathetic stimulation: raised intraocular pressure, urinary retention in BPH, worsened GI obstruction, tachycardia.

nodes.label: Norepinephrine reuptake
nodes.rationale: Reuptake into the presynaptic neuron is the primary mechanism ending norepinephrine's effects.

nodes.label: TCA anticholinergic and cardiac adverse effects
nodes.norm_label: tca anticholinergic and cardiac adverse effects
nodes.rationale: Quinidine-like cardiac conduction effects cause life-threatening arrhythmias in overdose; narrow therapeutic index so suicidal patients get limited quantities.

nodes.label: Antibiotics altering gut flora
nodes.rationale: Reduce enterohepatic recycling of estrogen, possibly diminishing oral contraceptive effectiveness.

nodes.label: Combination oral contraceptives
nodes.rationale: Active pills 21-24 days then 4-7 placebo days; withdrawal bleeding occurs in the hormone-free interval.

nodes.label: Contraceptive transdermal patch
nodes.rationale: Less effective in women over 90 kg; total estrogen exposure may be greater than with oral contraceptives.

nodes.label: Ethinyl estradiol
nodes.rationale: Less first-pass metabolism than natural estrogens, so effective orally at lower doses.

nodes.label: Hormonal contraceptive adverse effects
nodes.rationale: Severe effects (thromboembolism, MI, stroke) most common in women over 35 who smoke; progestin-only products preferred in older smokers.

nodes.label: Hormonal contraceptive mechanism of action
nodes.rationale: Estrogen negative feedback blunts FSH; progestin inhibits LH; progestin thickens cervical mucus; progestin withdrawal triggers bleeding in placebo week.

nodes.label: Progestin-only pills
nodes.rationale: Less effective, more irregular cycles; usable in breast-feeding (progestins do not affect milk production) or when estrogen is not tolerated or contraindicated.

nodes.label: Nilotinib
nodes.rationale: Avoid grapefruit juice and Seville oranges; QT prolongation.

nodes.label: Anticholinergic syndrome
nodes.rationale: Mnemonic: blind as a bat, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone, mad as a hatter, bloated as a toad, heart runs alone. Self-limiting; physostigmine only in life-threatening cases because of cholinergic excess.

nodes.label: Edrophonium
nodes.rationale: Quaternary amine, short 10-20 min action, peripheral only; use limited by newer agents. | Worsening weakness after the test dose means the AChE inhibitor dose is too high (depolarizing blockade).

nodes.label: Myasthenia gravis
nodes.rationale: Autoimmune disease: antibodies to nicotinic receptor at NMJ cause receptor degradation. | Autoimmune destruction of nicotinic receptors at the NMJ; AChE inhibitors raise ACh to activate the remaining receptors.

nodes.label: Neostigmine
nodes.rationale: Quaternary nitrogen makes it polar, poorly absorbed from the GI tract and unable to enter the CNS.

nodes.label: Physostigmine
nodes.rationale: Well absorbed from all sites, unlike other reversible inhibitors. | Tertiary amine, so it enters the CNS.

nodes.label: Reversible anticholinesterase agents
nodes.rationale: Prevent ACh breakdown so ACh accumulates and acts at all muscarinic and nicotinic receptors, NMJ and brain.

nodes.label: Drug
nodes.rationale: WHO 1966: any substance used to modify or explore physiological systems or pathological states for the benefit of the recipient.

nodes.label: Pharmacodynamics
nodes.rationale: What the drug does to the body: quantitative study of biological and therapeutic effect.

nodes.label: Pharmacokinetics
nodes.rationale: What the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion.

nodes.label: Pharmacology
nodes.rationale: Backbone of rational therapeutics; both a basic and an applied science.

nodes.label: Combination chemotherapy
nodes.rationale: Agents with different toxicities and mechanisms are combined at full doses for additive effect; agents with similar dose-limiting toxicities can be combined only by reducing doses. Intermittent schedule allows immune system recovery.

nodes.label: Maximal cell killing within tolerated toxicity
nodes.norm_label: maximal cell killing within tolerated toxicity

nodes.label: Alteplase
nodes.rationale: Fibrin selective: low affinity for free plasminogen but rapidly activates fibrin-bound plasminogen.

nodes.label: Streptokinase
nodes.rationale: Antigenic: antistreptococcal antibodies make retreatment less effective and unsafe; not preferred but used for low cost.

nodes.label: Thrombolytic drugs
nodes.rationale: Do not distinguish fibrin of a thrombus from fibrin of a hemostatic plug, so hemorrhage is the major adverse effect.

nodes.label: Asthma
nodes.rationale: Nonselective beta-blockers block beta-2 mediated bronchodilation.

nodes.norm_label: erratic absorption enhanced by fatty food

nodes.rationale: Not a CYP450 substrate; no drug interactions.

nodes.label: Caspofungin
nodes.rationale: Dose adjusted in moderate hepatic dysfunction; may need higher dose with inducers such as rifampin. | Requires a loading dose.

nodes.label: Echinocandins
nodes.rationale: Slow IV infusion needed because rapid infusion causes histamine-like flushing.

nodes.label: Micafungin
nodes.rationale: Only echinocandin that does not need a loading dose. | Not a CYP450 substrate; no drug interactions.

nodes.label: First-pass metabolism
nodes.rationale: Oral drugs pass through the portal circulation and liver first, so less unchanged drug reaches the systemic circulation.

nodes.label: Nitrate tolerance
nodes.rationale: Vessels desensitize to vasodilation; a daily 10 to 12 hour nitrate-free interval (at night; late afternoon in variant angina) restores sensitivity.

nodes.label: Nitric oxide, cGMP, myosin light chain dephosphorylation
nodes.norm_label: nitric oxide, cgmp, myosin light chain dephosphorylation

nodes.label: Rectal route
nodes.rationale: 50% of rectal drainage bypasses the portal circulation, minimizing hepatic biotransformation.

nodes.label: Sildenafil
nodes.rationale: Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors potentiate nitrates; the combination is contraindicated to prevent dangerous hypotension.

nodes.label: Sublingual and buccal routes
nodes.rationale: Rapid absorption; bypass the harsh GI environment and first-pass metabolism.

nodes.label: Antacids
nodes.rationale: Act by chemically neutralizing gastric acid, not through a receptor.

nodes.rationale: Subcutaneous route preferred because it causes less neuropathy.

nodes.label: Melphalan
nodes.rationale: Plasma levels vary between patients because of variable intestinal absorption and metabolism, so dose is adjusted by platelet and white cell counts.

nodes.label: Hepatitis C
nodes.rationale: RNA virus; preferred treatment is combination direct-acting antivirals chosen by genotype.

nodes.label: Nicotine
nodes.rationale: Low concentration stimulates the nicotinic receptor; high concentration blocks it. | Depolarizes autonomic ganglia, stimulating then paralysing all ganglia; no therapeutic benefit; the only depolarizing ganglionic blocker.

nodes.label: Partial agonist at neuronal nicotinic receptors

nodes.label: Varenicline
nodes.rationale: Not a controlled substance and carries lowest addiction risk; attenuates withdrawal; monitor psychiatric status.

nodes.label: Bipolar disorder
nodes.rationale: Antidepressants may switch the patient to manic behavior.

nodes.label: Furosemide
nodes.rationale: Oral bioavailability unpredictable (10-90%).

nodes.label: Lamotrigine
nodes.rationale: Slow titration needed because of rash risk that may progress to a life-threatening reaction; dose reduced when valproate is added since valproate lowers its clearance. | Best data for absence seizures among listed options. Pregnancy lowers its concentrations, so dosage may need to rise.

nodes.label: Lithium
nodes.rationale: Extremely low therapeutic index (0.5 to 1.4 mmol/L); levels above 2 mmol/L toxic; monitor levels. | Eliminated entirely by the kidney, needs no hepatic metabolism so is usable in hepatic impairment, but dose must be adjusted in renal impairment.

nodes.label: Lithium toxicity
nodes.rationale: Sodium depletion (low-salt diet, thiazides, loop diuretics, vomiting) and NSAIDs such as indomethacin raise lithium levels; contraindicated in first trimester and lactation.

nodes.label: Pregnancy-induced change in antiseizure drug pharmacokinetics
nodes.norm_label: pregnancy-induced change in antiseizure drug pharmacokinetics

nodes.label: Therapeutic drug monitoring
nodes.rationale: Not needed for prodrugs, irreversible drugs or drugs whose effect is easily measured (BP, blood sugar); used for low therapeutic index, saturable metabolism, variable metabolism, organ failure, noncompliance. | AED treatment is prophylactic, toxicity signs are subtle and no direct lab marker exists; not routine in controlled, nontoxic patients.

nodes.label: Trough levels
nodes.rationale: Plasma levels are taken before the next planned dose; urine concentration is unsuitable because urine volume varies.

nodes.label: Valproic acid
nodes.rationale: Many salt and extended-release forms exist, so the risk of medication errors is high. Divalproex was developed to improve GI tolerance. | Poor choice in women of child-bearing age; valproate in pregnancy harms children's cognitive abilities.

nodes.label: Vitamin K
nodes.rationale: Warfarin interferes with vitamin K use, so dietary vitamin K intake should be consistent.

nodes.label: Vitamin K1
nodes.rationale: Slow response (about 24 h) because new coagulation factors must be synthesized; use fresh frozen plasma if immediate hemostasis needed. Give IV slowly to avoid anaphylactoid reactions.

nodes.label: Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors II, VII, IX and X
nodes.norm_label: vitamin k-dependent clotting factors ii, vii, ix and x

nodes.label: Warfarin
nodes.rationale: Effect delayed 72-96 h because circulating clotting factors must be depleted; vitamin K reversal takes about 24 h because new factors must be made. Narrow therapeutic index, so INR monitored (goal 2-3).

nodes.label: Amlodipine
nodes.rationale: Very long half-life, so no sustained-release formulation needed (p. 325).

nodes.label: Calcium channel blockers
nodes.rationale: First-line in black patients; useful with asthma, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease because unlike beta-blockers they do not adversely affect these. Short-acting high doses avoided (MI risk from excessive vasodilation and reflex cardiac stimulation).

nodes.label: Crushing of oral dosage forms
nodes.rationale: Crushing extended-release or enteric-coated forms can dump a large bolus (overdose, e.g. nifedipine hypotension) then underdose later.

nodes.label: Dihydropyridines
nodes.rationale: Much greater affinity for vascular than cardiac calcium channels; little interaction with digoxin or warfarin.

nodes.label: Diltiazem
nodes.rationale: Less negative inotropic effect than verapamil.

nodes.label: Extended-release preparations
nodes.rationale: Slower absorption and prolonged action allow less frequent dosing and smaller peaks and troughs; useful for short half-life drugs.

nodes.label: Nifedipine
nodes.rationale: Short-acting dihydropyridines should be avoided in CAD: increased mortality after MI and more acute MI in hypertensive patients.

nodes.label: GnRH analogs
nodes.rationale: Continuous (non-pulsatile) administration down-regulates GnRH receptors, suppressing FSH and LH; in men an initial testosterone rise causes bone pain.

nodes.label: Leuprolide
nodes.rationale: Androgen levels may first rise (tumor flare) then fall to castration levels.

nodes.label: Clozapine
nodes.rationale: Restricted to refractory patients (10-20% of schizophrenia) because of serious adverse effects; needs frequent white cell count monitoring.

nodes.label: Quetiapine
nodes.rationale: Low EPS risk may relate to short time bound to the D2 receptor; strong H1 blockade makes it sedating, sometimes used off-label as a hypnotic.

nodes.label: Second-generation antipsychotics
nodes.rationale: Lower EPS but higher metabolic risk; used first-line for schizophrenia to avoid EPS.

nodes.norm_label: increased norepinephrine and dopamine release and reuptake inhibition

nodes.label: Obesity
nodes.rationale: Effective drugs must give at least 5% greater weight reduction than placebo.

nodes.label: Abacavir
nodes.rationale: Rapidly appearing, severe and potentially fatal reactions on rechallenge; HLA-B*5701 screening available. Same-analog NRTIs (e.g., zidovudine and stavudine) show cross-resistance and antagonism.

nodes.label: Alcohol dehydrogenase and glucuronyl transferase metabolism

nodes.label: Cetuximab
nodes.rationale: Rash is equated with increased response.

nodes.label: Itraconazole

nodes.label: Adherence (compliance)

nodes.community_name: Factors affecting drug response and related
nodes.rationale: Aging raises body fat and lowers total body water, so water-soluble drugs reach higher concentrations and fat-soluble drugs have longer half-lives; low albumin raises free drug.

nodes.rationale: Renal function falls about 1% per year and about 50% in the elderly; dosage of renally excreted drugs needs adapting once more than 50% of function is lost.

nodes.label: COX-1
nodes.rationale: Constitutive enzyme: gastric cytoprotection, vascular homeostasis, platelet aggregation, reproductive and kidney function.

nodes.label: COX-2
nodes.rationale: Elevated at sites of chronic disease and inflammation; larger substrate channel allows selective inhibitors.

nodes.label: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis in HIV with CD4 below 200

nodes.label: Culture before first antibiotic dose
nodes.rationale: Otherwise a negative culture cannot be told apart from an antibiotic effect.

nodes.label: Empiric antimicrobial therapy
nodes.rationale: Delay could be fatal in the critically ill; switch to narrow-spectrum drugs within 48 to 72 hours per culture and sensitivity.

nodes.label: Sequential blockade of tetrahydrofolic acid synthesis
nodes.norm_label: sequential blockade of tetrahydrofolic acid synthesis

nodes.label: Bethanechol
nodes.rationale: Carbamoyl ester resistant to AChE; lacks nicotinic action; about 1-hour duration.

nodes.label: Metabotropic receptors
nodes.rationale: G protein-coupled; act through second messengers (adenylyl cyclase system, calcium/phosphatidylinositol system), not directly on ion channels.

nodes.label: Muscarinic receptors
nodes.rationale: G protein-coupled; M1 and M3 act via phospholipase C (IP3, DAG); M2 in heart inhibits adenylyl cyclase and raises K+ conductance.

nodes.label: Competes with estrogen for estrogen receptors
nodes.norm_label: competes with estrogen for estrogen receptors

nodes.label: Tamoxifen
nodes.rationale: Estrogenic in endometrium, so hyperplasia and malignancy reported; CYP2D6 polymorphism can reduce active metabolite. | Estrogen antagonist in breast but agonist in bone and endometrium.

nodes.label: Neuraminidase inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Preferred approach to influenza is vaccination; given within 24-48 h of symptoms they modestly reduce intensity and duration.

nodes.label: Clomiphene
nodes.rationale: Partial estrogen agonist blocking estrogen negative feedback on hypothalamus, raising GnRH and gonadotropins to stimulate ovulation. | SERM that blocks estrogen negative feedback, raising GnRH and gonadotropins and stimulating ovulation.

nodes.label: Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
nodes.norm_label: deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

nodes.label: Raloxifene
nodes.rationale: Estrogen agonist in bone; does not stimulate endometrium so no endometrial cancer risk; lowers total cholesterol and LDL. | Does not increase endometrial cancer risk; lowers breast cancer risk in high-risk women and LDL; raises venous thromboembolism risk.

nodes.label: Selective estrogen receptor modulators
nodes.rationale: Selective agonism or antagonism of estrogen receptors depending on tissue type.

nodes.label: Pegfilgrastim
nodes.rationale: Pegylated G-CSF with longer half-life; given as a single dose, ANC monitoring not needed.

nodes.label: Figure 37.3 anthelmintics to avoid in pregnancy
nodes.norm_label: figure 37.3 anthelmintics to avoid in pregnancy

nodes.label: Postmarketing surveillance
nodes.rationale: Premarketing trials are short, small and selective, so rare ADRs (under 1%) and long-term ADRs are missed.

nodes.label: Blockade of Ca2+ release from sarcoplasmic reticulum
nodes.norm_label: blockade of ca2+ release from sarcoplasmic reticulum

nodes.label: Malignant hyperthermia
nodes.rationale: Excitation-contraction coupling defect, often autosomal dominant; triggered by halogenated anesthetics or succinylcholine.

nodes.label: Succinylcholine
nodes.rationale: Only depolarizing relaxant; Phase I fasciculations then Phase II desensitization with flaccid paralysis; short action from plasma cholinesterase hydrolysis.

nodes.label: Cisatracurium
nodes.rationale: Organ-independent Hofmann elimination, so suitable in multisystem organ failure.

nodes.label: Nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers
nodes.rationale: Compete with ACh at nicotinic receptors without stimulating them; at high doses block the endplate ion channel, so cholinesterase inhibitors reverse them less well.

nodes.label: Order of muscle paralysis and recovery
nodes.norm_label: order of muscle paralysis and recovery
nodes.rationale: Small fast muscles of face and eye first, then fingers, limbs, neck, trunk, intercostals, diaphragm last; recovery in reverse.

nodes.label: Sugammadex
nodes.rationale: Traps the blocker 1:1, rendering it water soluble; reverses shallow and profound blockade.

nodes.label: Acitretin
nodes.rationale: Teratogenic potential is long, so women must avoid pregnancy for at least 3 years after use.

nodes.label: Diffusion hypoxia
nodes.rationale: Rapid nitrous oxide exit retards oxygen uptake in recovery; overcome with high inspired oxygen.

nodes.label: Nitrous oxide
nodes.rationale: Cannot alone produce general anesthesia because its MAC cannot be reached with survivable oxygen. | Replaces nitrogen in air spaces faster than nitrogen leaves, expanding pneumothorax or raising sinus and middle ear pressure.

nodes.label: Continuous infusion regimen
nodes.rationale: Css is proportional to infusion rate and inversely proportional to clearance; infusion rate does not change time to steady state.

nodes.label: Fixed-dose regimens
nodes.rationale: Smaller doses at shorter intervals reduce fluctuation but change neither Css nor the time to reach it.

nodes.label: Half-life
nodes.rationale: Applies only to first-order kinetics; independent of dose and dosing interval; steady state in four to five half-lives.

nodes.label: Renal disease
nodes.rationale: Poor excretion prolongs half-life, so dosage must be reduced to avoid toxicity.

nodes.label: Steady-state concentration
nodes.rationale: Reached when rate of elimination equals rate of administration; takes about 3.3 half-lives for 90% and four to five half-lives overall.

nodes.label: Total body clearance
nodes.rationale: CLtotal = CLhepatic + CLrenal + CLpulmonary + CLother.

nodes.label: Bioequivalence
nodes.rationale: Brand switching of phenytoin, lithium and digoxin may change bioavailability and need dose adjustment.

nodes.label: Effect of pH and pKa on absorption
nodes.norm_label: effect of ph and pka on absorption
nodes.rationale: Only the uncharged form crosses membranes; the ratio of forms depends on site pH and pKa.

nodes.norm_label: inhibit extra-adrenal estrogen synthesis from androstenedione

nodes.label: Ergotamine
nodes.rationale: Contraindicated in peripheral vascular disease because it is a significant vasoconstrictor.

nodes.rationale: Conjugation (glucuronidation is most common) makes polar, usually inactive products; exception morphine-6-glucuronide is more potent than morphine. | Conjugation reactions make phase I metabolites more polar; sulfation and glucuronidation are the most common.

nodes.label: Alpha-1 blockers
nodes.rationale: No longer initial treatment for hypertension because of weaker outcome data and side effects; slow titration needed because of reflex tachycardia and postural hypotension at start.

nodes.label: Alpha-blockers
nodes.rationale: Blocking alpha-1 lowers peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure, causing reflex tachycardia.

nodes.label: Doxazosin
nodes.rationale: Longest acting of these; metabolites appear in feces.

nodes.label: First-dose effect
nodes.rationale: First dose may cause exaggerated orthostatic hypotension and syncope; minimized by giving one-third to one-fourth dose at bedtime.

nodes.label: First-dose syncope
nodes.rationale: Start at a low dose with gradual increases; give dose at bedtime.

nodes.label: Midodrine
nodes.rationale: Prodrug converted to desglymidodrine; doses within 4 hours of bedtime avoided to prevent supine hypertension.

nodes.label: Receptor down-regulation
nodes.rationale: Occurs when receptor activation is greater than normal from continuous agonist exposure.

nodes.label: Receptor up-regulation
nodes.rationale: Occurs when receptor activation is lower than normal, e.g. continuous exposure to an antagonist such as prazosin.

nodes.label: Tamsulosin
nodes.rationale: Selective alpha-1A antagonist; fewer cardiovascular effects because it spares alpha-1B receptors in blood vessels. | Selective for alpha1A in prostate, less for alpha1B in vessels, so little effect on blood pressure

nodes.label: Estradiol
nodes.rationale: Most potent estrogen secreted by the ovary; principal estrogen premenopause; low oral bioavailability from first-pass metabolism.

nodes.label: Estradiol valerate
nodes.rationale: Prodrug cleaved rapidly to estradiol and valeric acid.

nodes.label: Estrogens
nodes.rationale: Estrogen therapy for prostate cancer is not used because of side effects and safer alternatives.

nodes.label: Estrogen adverse effects
nodes.rationale: Nausea, breast tenderness, thromboembolism, MI, hypertension, fluid retention, headache; endometrial cancer risk offset by a progestogen.

nodes.label: Intracellular steroid hormone receptors
nodes.rationale: Steroid-receptor complex binds DNA response elements with coactivators to regulate transcription; effects are receptor and tissue specific.

nodes.label: Enteric-coated preparations
nodes.community_name: Past Paper Answers document and related
nodes.rationale: Coating protects acid-labile drugs, spares the stomach from irritants and delays onset to a site in the GI tract.

nodes.label: Iontophoresis
nodes.community_name: Past Paper Answers document and related
nodes.rationale: Not covered by Lippincott or Katzung (Katzung p. 115 names it once); every point on it in the answer file is tagged [not in book].

nodes.label: Oral route
nodes.community_name: Past Paper Answers document and related
nodes.rationale: Most common, convenient and economical route; overdose can be countered with antidotes such as activated charcoal; but low gastric pH inactivates some drugs.

nodes.label: Drospirenone
nodes.rationale: Antimineralocorticoid effect raises serum potassium.

nodes.label: Mifepristone
nodes.rationale: Progesterone antagonist; ends pregnancy by blocking progesterone needed to maintain it.

nodes.label: Progesterone
nodes.rationale: Not used as a contraceptive because rapid metabolism gives low bioavailability; promotes secretory endometrium; luteal-phase levels inhibit gonadotropin and prevent ovulation.

nodes.label: Progestins
nodes.rationale: Synthetic progestogens, more stable to first-pass metabolism, allowing lower oral doses.

nodes.label: Progestin adverse effects
nodes.rationale: Headache, depression, weight gain, libido changes.

nodes.label: Sex hormones
nodes.rationale: Synthesized from cholesterol; aromatization is the last step in estrogen synthesis.

nodes.rationale: Five-subunit ligand-gated ion channel; two ACh molecules open it and let Na+ in; found in CNS, adrenal medulla, ganglia (NN) and NMJ (NM).

nodes.rationale: Anion-exchange resins; contraindicated if triglycerides >400 mg/dL because they can raise triglycerides; little effect in homozygous type IIA lacking LDL receptors.

nodes.rationale: Modest LDL-C lowering (18-23%), so used as adjunct to maximal statin or in statin intolerance; avoid in moderate-to-severe hepatic insufficiency.

nodes.label: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Osmotic diuresis may lower systolic BP, but not indicated for hypertension.

nodes.rationale: Developed because of cisplatin's severe toxicity; used when patients cannot be vigorously hydrated, or have kidney dysfunction or neuro/ototoxicity risk.

nodes.rationale: Defective LDL receptors; homozygotes lack receptors and respond poorly to statins.

nodes.label: Direct-acting antivirals
nodes.rationale: Combination of agents targeting different life-cycle stages suppresses wild-type and resistant virus.

nodes.label: NS5B polymerase inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Well tolerated with few adverse effects.

nodes.label: Indirect-acting adrenergic agonists
nodes.rationale: Cause release, inhibit reuptake, or inhibit degradation of norepinephrine; do not act directly on postsynaptic receptors.

nodes.label: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Last-line agents because of drug-drug and drug-food interactions; 2 week washout needed when switching.

nodes.label: Selegiline
nodes.rationale: Metabolized to methamphetamine and amphetamine, so can cause insomnia if given after mid-afternoon; loses MAO-B selectivity at high doses

nodes.label: Tyramine
nodes.rationale: Normally oxidized by MAO in the gut; with MAO inhibitors it can precipitate serious vasopressor episodes (aged cheese, Chianti).

nodes.label: Antipsychotics
nodes.rationale: Not curative; reduce intensity of hallucinations and delusions; involve trade-off between benefit and wide range of adverse effects.

nodes.label: Antipsychotic maintenance treatment
nodes.rationale: Lower doses for first-episode patients and the elderly; two or more psychotic episodes need maintenance for at least 5 years.

nodes.label: Aripiprazole
nodes.rationale: As a partial dopamine agonist it inhibits overactive and stimulates underactive pathways, with a small risk of extrapyramidal effects.

nodes.label: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia

nodes.label: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
nodes.rationale: Duration 2 to 4 weeks (some 6 to 12 weeks); used for outpatients and those nonadherent to oral drugs.

nodes.rationale: Enhances action when dopamine is low and blocks it when dopamine is high.

nodes.label: Schizophrenia
nodes.rationale: Chronic psychosis with delusions, hallucinations and disturbed thought; about 1% of population; possibly dysfunction of mesolimbic or mesocortical dopaminergic pathways.

nodes.label: Corticosteroids
nodes.rationale: High-dose IV for 3 to 5 days ends relapses faster but gives no long-term benefit

nodes.label: HPA axis suppression
nodes.rationale: Occurs with large doses for more than 2 weeks; alternate-day dosing lets the axis recover; abrupt stopping can cause fatal acute adrenal insufficiency so doses are tapered.

nodes.label: Hydrocortisone
nodes.rationale: Two-thirds of daily dose in the morning and one-third in the afternoon to mimic diurnal cortisol variation.

nodes.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Turning off checkpoints allows tumor attack but also unchecked autoimmune response against normal tissue.

nodes.label: Parasympathetic nervous system
nodes.rationale: Craniosacral outflow (CN III, VII, IX, X; S2-S4); long preganglionic, short postganglionic fibers; one-to-one connections give discrete responses; never discharges as a whole.

nodes.label: Somatic nervous system
nodes.rationale: Single myelinated motor neuron with no ganglia gives faster responses than the ANS.

nodes.label: Sympathetic nervous system
nodes.rationale: Thoracolumbar (T1-L2) outflow; short preganglionic, long postganglionic fibers; highly branched so it discharges diffusely as a unit.

nodes.rationale: Abdominal wall is common; back of arm, outer thigh, upper buttocks also used; rotate sites but keep same general location at the same time each day.

nodes.label: Insulin lispro
nodes.rationale: Rapid-acting, onset 15-30 minutes; mimics mealtime insulin release and controls postprandial glucose.

nodes.label: Insulin storage

nodes.label: Lipodystrophy

nodes.label: NPH insulin

nodes.label: Parenteral route

nodes.label: Rapid-acting insulin analogs

nodes.label: Regular insulin

nodes.label: Somogyi effect
nodes.rationale: Morning hyperglycemia due to excessive exogenous insulin; diagnose by plasma glucose between 3 and 5 a.m.

nodes.label: Subcutaneous route
nodes.rationale: Not for tissue-irritating drugs because severe pain and necrosis may occur.

nodes.label: Type 1 diabetes
