nodes.rationale: Given IM to the mother within 48 hours before premature delivery to accelerate fetal lung maturation.

nodes.label: Cortisol
nodes.rationale: Anti-inflammatory, increases gluconeogenesis and protein breakdown; negative feedback on ACTH.

nodes.label: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
nodes.rationale: Suppressed intestinal calcium absorption, inhibited bone formation and decreased sex hormone synthesis.

nodes.label: Hypothalamic-pituitary regulation
nodes.rationale: Anterior pituitary hormones are peptides given IM, subcutaneously or intranasally because proteolytic enzymes destroy them orally.

nodes.label: Intracellular corticosteroid receptor
nodes.rationale: Acts as a transcription factor, so some effects take hours to days.

nodes.label: Ketoconazole
nodes.rationale: Oral use rarely today because of severe liver injury, adrenal insufficiency and interactions.

nodes.label: Figure 26.5 Routes of administration of corticosteroids
nodes.norm_label: figure 26.5 routes of administration of corticosteroids

nodes.label: Figure 26.6 Effects of long-term corticosteroid therapy
nodes.norm_label: figure 26.6 effects of long-term corticosteroid therapy

nodes.label: Figure 27.3 Drugs that can contribute to bone loss
nodes.norm_label: figure 27.3 drugs that can contribute to bone loss

nodes.label: Azithromycin
nodes.rationale: Considered safe in pregnancy

nodes.label: Doxycycline
nodes.rationale: Preferred because eliminated via bile into feces

nodes.label: Inhibition of protein synthesis in parasite plastid
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of protein synthesis in parasite plastid

nodes.label: Prevention of tRNA binding to mRNA-ribosome complex
nodes.norm_label: prevention of trna binding to mrna-ribosome complex

nodes.label: Tigecycline
nodes.rationale: Low plasma concentrations

nodes.label: Tooth discoloration and bone growth stunting
nodes.norm_label: tooth discoloration and bone growth stunting

nodes.label: Amphetamine overdose
nodes.rationale: Indirect agonist activates both alpha and beta receptors, so only a drug blocking both (labetalol) relieves the cardiovascular effects

nodes.label: Direct-acting vasodilators
nodes.rationale: Reflex cardiac stimulation and renin rise cause tachycardia and salt/water retention; given with a beta-blocker and a diuretic to counter these.

nodes.label: Hypertension in pregnancy
nodes.rationale: Methyldopa, beta-blockers, vasodilators preferred; long-term beta-blockers cause fetal growth retardation; ACE inhibitors and ARBs strongly contraindicated.

nodes.label: Hypertensive emergency
nodes.rationale: Systolic >180 or diastolic >120 mm Hg with target organ damage; without organ damage it is hypertensive urgency.

nodes.label: Labetalol
nodes.rationale: Alpha1 blockade causes vasodilation, so no reflex tachycardia; useful where raised peripheral resistance is undesirable

nodes.label: Modification of microfilariae for immune elimination
nodes.norm_label: modification of microfilariae for immune elimination

nodes.label: Cilostazol
nodes.rationale: PDE III inhibitors increase mortality in advanced heart failure, so cilostazol is contraindicated in heart failure.

nodes.label: Clopidogrel
nodes.rationale: Prodrug needing CYP2C19; poor metabolizers have a diminished antiplatelet effect. | A prodrug that needs CYP2C19 for conversion to its active metabolite. | Prodrug activated by CYP2C19; poor metabolizers respond less and should get prasugrel or ticagrelor.

nodes.label: Dipyridamole
nodes.rationale: Vasodilating action may worsen ischemia (coronary steal) in unstable angina.

nodes.label: P2Y12 receptor antagonists
nodes.rationale: Block ADP binding to P2Y12 so GP IIb/IIIa receptors are not activated for fibrinogen binding. No antidote for the prolonged bleeding.

nodes.label: Ticagrelor
nodes.rationale: Binds P2Y12 reversibly, so antiplatelet effect stops when doses are missed.

nodes.label: Ticlopidine
nodes.rationale: Reserved for patients intolerant of other therapies because of life-threatening hematologic reactions.

nodes.label: Cyclosporine
nodes.rationale: High incidence of elevated hepatic transaminases with caspofungin.

nodes.label: Prednisone
nodes.rationale: Preferred in pregnancy: prodrug not converted to prednisolone in the fetal liver; placental enzymes convert maternal prednisolone back to prednisone.

nodes.label: Acetaminophen overdose
nodes.rationale: Metabolic pathways saturate; glutathione is depleted so NAPQI is not detoxified.

nodes.label: N-acetylcysteine
nodes.rationale: Most effective within 8 hours of acetaminophen ingestion; still given after 24 hours; oral form unpalatable and may cause vomiting.

nodes.label: Sulfhydryl groups break disulfide bonds of mucoprotein
nodes.norm_label: sulfhydryl groups break disulfide bonds of mucoprotein

nodes.label: Long-acting beta-2 agonists
nodes.rationale: Not recommended as asthma monotherapy because of increased asthma-related deaths; highly efficacious combined with an inhaled corticosteroid. | Monotherapy is contraindicated; use only with an asthma controller such as an inhaled corticosteroid

nodes.label: Acyclovir
nodes.rationale: Phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase (over 100-fold faster than host enzyme), so virus-infected cells are most susceptible.

nodes.label: Altered thymidine kinase and DNA polymerase resistance
nodes.norm_label: altered thymidine kinase and dna polymerase resistance

nodes.label: Ganciclovir
nodes.rationale: Carcinogenic and teratogenic; boxed warning for use in pregnancy.

nodes.label: Viral DNA chain termination by acyclovir triphosphate
nodes.norm_label: viral dna chain termination by acyclovir triphosphate

nodes.label: Affinity
nodes.rationale: Higher Kd means weaker binding and lower affinity.

nodes.label: Albuterol
nodes.rationale: SABA of choice in acute asthma because more beta-2 selective than metaproterenol.

nodes.label: Competitive antagonist
nodes.rationale: Overcome by raising agonist concentration; shifts the curve right (higher EC50) without changing Emax.

nodes.label: Efficacy
nodes.rationale: More clinically useful than potency: a drug with greater efficacy is more therapeutically beneficial than one that is more potent.

nodes.label: Irreversible antagonist
nodes.rationale: Binds covalently, permanently reducing receptor number, so Emax falls and more agonist cannot overcome it.

nodes.label: Spare receptors
nodes.rationale: About 99% of insulin receptors are spare, but only 5-10% of cardiac beta-adrenoceptors, so the failing heart has little functional reserve.

nodes.label: Folic acid analog inhibiting folinic acid production
nodes.norm_label: folic acid analog inhibiting folinic acid production

nodes.label: Folic acid and vitamin B12 supplementation
nodes.norm_label: folic acid and vitamin b12 supplementation

nodes.label: Maintenance of remission in Crohn disease
nodes.norm_label: maintenance of remission in crohn disease

nodes.label: Methotrexate
nodes.rationale: Inhibition of DHFR is reversed only by a 1000-fold excess of dihydrofolate or by leucovorin, which bypasses the blocked enzyme and replenishes the folate pool.

nodes.label: Metronidazole
nodes.rationale: Phenobarbital (CYP inducer) speeds its metabolism and cimetidine (inhibitor) prolongs half-life; with alcohol it causes a disulfiram-like reaction.

nodes.label: Prodrug activated by nitro group reduction
nodes.norm_label: prodrug activated by nitro group reduction

nodes.label: Tinidazole
nodes.rationale: Longer half-life (12 h) allows single 2 g dose.

nodes.label: Antiretroviral therapy
nodes.rationale: Combination of drugs used because it suppresses HIV replication and restores CD4 count; initial therapy is two NRTIs plus an integrase inhibitor, an NNRTI or a boosted PI.

nodes.label: Atazanavir
nodes.rationale: Requires an acidic environment for absorption, so unboosted atazanavir is contraindicated with proton-pump inhibitors and doses are spaced from H2-blockers and antacids.

nodes.label: Inhibition of proviral DNA insertion into host genome
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of proviral dna insertion into host genome

nodes.label: Ritonavir
nodes.rationale: Used only as a booster: low-dose ritonavir inhibits CYP3A, raising bioavailability and Cmin of the second PI, allowing longer dosing intervals and helping prevent resistance.

nodes.label: First trimester Plasmodium falciparum malaria in pregnancy
nodes.norm_label: first trimester plasmodium falciparum malaria in pregnancy

nodes.label: Malaria prevention and treatment for travelers
nodes.norm_label: malaria prevention and treatment for travelers

nodes.label: Sodium channel block with potassium and calcium block
nodes.norm_label: sodium channel block with potassium and calcium block

nodes.label: Antidepressant discontinuation syndrome
nodes.rationale: Fluoxetine has lowest risk because of long half-life and active metabolite; taper gradually.

nodes.label: Buspirone
nodes.rationale: Slow onset (3-6 weeks) so not for as-needed treatment; no sedation, anticonvulsant or muscle-relaxant effect; does not potentiate alcohol.

nodes.label: Obsessive-compulsive, panic and other anxiety disorders
nodes.norm_label: obsessive-compulsive, panic and other anxiety disorders

nodes.label: Rufinamide
nodes.rationale: Can shorten the QT interval, so contraindicated in familial short QT syndrome.

nodes.label: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Largely replaced TCAs and MAOIs as drugs of choice because of different adverse effects and relative safety in overdose.

nodes.label: Sodium channel blockade
nodes.rationale: Prevents the transient Na+ permeability increase needed for an action potential, so sensation is not transmitted.

nodes.label: Atypical femur fracture
nodes.rationale: Risk rises with long-term use, so a drug holiday is considered after 5 years of oral bisphosphonates or 3 years of zoledronic acid.

nodes.label: Esophagitis
nodes.rationale: Patients stay upright after oral bisphosphonates to limit esophageal irritation.

nodes.label: Hormonal regulators of calcium and phosphate homeostasis
nodes.norm_label: hormonal regulators of calcium and phosphate homeostasis

nodes.label: Injectable progestin contraception
nodes.rationale: Medroxyprogesterone acetate every 3 months; bone loss risk, so not continued over 2 years unless other options not tolerated; delayed return to fertility.

nodes.label: Medroxyprogesterone acetate
nodes.rationale: Bone loss; not continued beyond 2 years if possible.

nodes.label: Osteoporosis
nodes.rationale: Estrogen decreases bone resorption but not formation; bisphosphonates preferred over estrogen.

nodes.label: Teriparatide
nodes.rationale: Anabolic; lifetime use limited to 2 years; osteosarcoma seen in rats.

nodes.label: Alzheimer disease
nodes.rationale: Deficiency of cholinergic neurons and low CNS ACh; anticholinesterases delay but cannot stop progression.

nodes.label: Alzheimer's disease
nodes.rationale: Senile plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and loss of cholinergic cortical neurons; drugs are only palliative

nodes.label: Mirabegron
nodes.rationale: May raise blood pressure so avoided in uncontrolled hypertension; raises digoxin levels and inhibits CYP2D6 (e.g., metoprolol).

nodes.label: NMDA receptor antagonism
nodes.rationale: Blocks excessive Ca2+ influx, preventing excitotoxic neuron damage

nodes.label: Quaternary ammonium antimuscarinics
nodes.rationale: Less lipid soluble, absorbed only 10 to 30 percent and do not cross the blood-brain barrier; tertiary antagonists are well absorbed and reach the brain.

nodes.label: Rivastigmine
nodes.rationale: Only agent approved for Parkinson's dementia and only transdermal AChE inhibitor; no CYP450 interactions

nodes.label: Tacrine
nodes.rationale: Replaced by other agents because of hepatotoxicity.

nodes.label: Trospium
nodes.rationale: Quaternary, minimally crosses the blood-brain barrier, so preferred for overactive bladder in dementia.

nodes.label: Induction therapy
nodes.rationale: Powerfully suppresses immune system at time of transplant so new organ can function and early rejection is prevented

nodes.label: Premedication with corticosteroids, acetaminophen and antihistamines
nodes.norm_label: premedication with corticosteroids, acetaminophen and antihistamines

nodes.label: Inhibition of transport of essential elements
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of transport of essential elements

nodes.label: Low oral bioavailability from first-pass metabolism
nodes.norm_label: low oral bioavailability from first-pass metabolism

nodes.label: Terbinafine
nodes.rationale: Better tolerated, shorter course (about 3 months) and more effective than itraconazole or griseofulvin for onychomycosis.

nodes.label: Tolnaftate
nodes.rationale: Not effective against Candida.

nodes.label: Whitfield's ointment
nodes.rationale: Benzoic acid with salicylic acid 2:1: fungistatic plus keratolytic.

nodes.label: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
nodes.rationale: Dangerous because second-line drugs are few, toxic and expensive, and it can spread to others if not treated properly.

nodes.label: Abiraterone
nodes.rationale: Given with prednisone to lessen mineralocorticoid excess caused by CYP17 inhibition.

nodes.label: ACE inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Cannot be combined with ARBs or aliskiren: similar mechanisms and adverse effects. Serum creatinine rise up to 30% above baseline is acceptable. | Dry cough and angioedema come from raised bradykinin; contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal malformations).

nodes.label: Aliskiren
nodes.rationale: Acts earlier in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system than ACE inhibitors or ARBs; metabolized by CYP3A4 with many interactions.

nodes.label: Angioedema
nodes.rationale: Rare but life-threatening; may be due to increased bradykinin.

nodes.label: Angiotensin II receptor blockers
nodes.rationale: Do not raise bradykinin, so cough and angioedema risk is much lower than with ACE inhibitors.

nodes.label: Angiotensin receptor blockers
nodes.rationale: Used when ACE inhibitor is indicated but not tolerated because of cough; do not produce cough. | Do not raise bradykinin, so far less cough and angioedema than ACE inhibitors.

nodes.label: Beta-blockers with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity
nodes.rationale: Partial agonist effect means less fall in heart rate and fewer lipid/carbohydrate disturbances; not used for stable angina or arrhythmias

nodes.label: Block ACE conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II
nodes.norm_label: block ace conversion of angiotensin i to angiotensin ii

nodes.label: Diabetic nephropathy
nodes.rationale: ACE inhibitors reduce intraglomerular pressure through efferent arteriolar vasodilation.

nodes.label: Dry cough
nodes.rationale: Due to raised bradykinin and substance P in the lungs; up to 10% of patients, more in women; resolves within days of stopping.

nodes.label: Fosinopril
nodes.rationale: Only ACE inhibitor not eliminated primarily by the kidneys, so no dose adjustment in renal impairment.

nodes.label: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system
nodes.rationale: Kidney provides long-term BP control by altering blood volume. | Compensatory activation retains sodium and water and raises afterload; angiotensin II and aldosterone cause remodeling and fibrosis.

nodes.label: Sympathetic nervous system activation
nodes.rationale: Raises heart rate, contractility and preload to sustain output, but increases cardiac workload and worsens function long term.

nodes.label: Benign prostatic hyperplasia in enlarged prostate
nodes.norm_label: benign prostatic hyperplasia in enlarged prostate

nodes.label: Finasteride
nodes.rationale: Should not be used or handled in pregnancy as it can cause hypospadias in a male fetus; must be continued to keep benefit.

nodes.label: Inhibition of 5-alpha reductase types I and II
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of 5-alpha reductase types i and ii

nodes.label: Inhibition of testosterone conversion to dihydrotestosterone
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of testosterone conversion to dihydrotestosterone

nodes.label: Methyltestosterone
nodes.rationale: 17-alpha alkylation reduces hepatic metabolism and allows oral use.

nodes.label: Testosterone
nodes.rationale: Ineffective orally because of first-pass inactivation, so given transdermal, topical, buccal, implant or as IM esters.

nodes.label: Absorbed in duodenum as ferrous form
nodes.norm_label: absorbed in duodenum as ferrous form

nodes.label: Absorption depends on body iron stores
nodes.norm_label: absorption depends on body iron stores

nodes.label: Carbonyl iron
nodes.rationale: 100% elemental iron

nodes.label: Ferric ammonium citrate
nodes.rationale: 18% elemental iron

nodes.label: Ferrous gluconate
nodes.rationale: 12% elemental iron

nodes.label: Ferrous sulfate
nodes.rationale: 20% elemental iron (30% anhydrous); 325 mg gives about 65 mg

nodes.label: Polysaccharide-iron complex
nodes.rationale: 150 mg gives 150 mg elemental iron; extended release, once daily

nodes.label: Fosphenytoin
nodes.rationale: Prodrug usable IM and IV; phenytoin sodium must never be given IM because it causes tissue damage and necrosis.

nodes.label: Phenytoin
nodes.rationale: Many interactions; dizziness may lead to falls, cognitive and bone health problems in the elderly.

nodes.label: Saturation kinetics
nodes.rationale: Hepatic hydroxylation saturates, so small dose increases cause large plasma concentration rises.

nodes.label: Carbidopa
nodes.rationale: Prevents peripheral conversion of levodopa, lowering the levodopa dose four- to five-fold and reducing peripheral side effects

nodes.label: Catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibition
nodes.rationale: Lowers 3-O-methyldopa, which competes with levodopa for transport into the CNS

nodes.label: Entacapone
nodes.rationale: Acts only in the periphery and lacks tolcapone's liver toxicity, so has largely replaced tolcapone

nodes.label: Levodopa
nodes.rationale: Dopamine cannot cross the blood-brain barrier but its precursor levodopa is actively transported; should be taken on an empty stomach as protein competes for transport; never stopped suddenly

nodes.label: Parkinson's disease
nodes.rationale: Loss of dopamine inhibition of cholinergic neurons leaves relative acetylcholine overactivity; therapy restores dopamine/acetylcholine balance but does not stop degeneration

nodes.label: Tolcapone
nodes.rationale: Fulminating hepatic necrosis: reserved for patients in whom other modalities failed, with liver monitoring

nodes.label: Azole resistance
nodes.rationale: Mutations in 14-alpha demethylase gene, efflux pumps, reduced ergosterol.

nodes.label: Fluconazole
nodes.rationale: First triazole; least active; no role in aspergillosis or zygomycosis; resistance in C. krusei and C. glabrata.

nodes.label: Inhibition of lanosterol to ergosterol conversion
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of lanosterol to ergosterol conversion

nodes.label: Isavuconazole
nodes.rationale: Given as prodrug isavuconazonium, hydrolysed by blood esterases.

nodes.label: Posaconazole
nodes.rationale: Minimal CYP metabolism; eliminated mostly by UGT glucuronidation.

nodes.label: Nimesulide
nodes.rationale: Adding paracetamol to nimesulide gives no gain in efficacy but increases hepatotoxicity.

nodes.label: Chronic suppression of urinary tract infections
nodes.norm_label: chronic suppression of urinary tract infections

nodes.label: Inhibition of DNA and RNA synthesis
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of dna and rna synthesis

nodes.label: Ascending loop of Henle
nodes.rationale: Water-impermeable; reabsorbs 25-30% of filtered NaCl, so drugs here have the greatest diuretic effect.

nodes.label: Chlorthalidone
nodes.rationale: About twice as potent as hydrochlorothiazide; half-life 50-60 hours.

nodes.label: Decreased peripheral resistance
nodes.rationale: With long-term thiazide treatment plasma volume normalizes but hypotensive effect persists through decreased peripheral resistance.

nodes.label: Digoxin
nodes.rationale: Digoxin and K+ compete for the same site on Na+/K+-ATPase, so low K+ increases binding and toxicity.

nodes.label: Hypokalemia
nodes.rationale: More Na+ delivered to the distal tubule is exchanged for K+; low-sodium diets blunt the loss.

nodes.label: Idiopathic hypercalciuria and calcium oxalate stones
nodes.norm_label: idiopathic hypercalciuria and calcium oxalate stones

nodes.label: Loop diuretics
nodes.rationale: Highest-efficacy diuretics; sigmoidal dose-response with threshold and ceiling, so adjust dosing frequency rather than dose. Work even in poor renal function.

nodes.label: Osmotic diuretics
nodes.rationale: Cause aquaresis with little Na+ loss, so not useful where Na+ is retained.

nodes.label: Thiazide diuretics
nodes.rationale: Low-ceiling diuretics: higher doses give no more diuresis. Must be secreted into the tubule at the proximal tubule to work, so reduced renal function reduces effect. Do not usually cross-react in sulfonamide antimicrobial allergy.

nodes.label: Calcium permeability increase in worm membrane
nodes.norm_label: calcium permeability increase in worm membrane

nodes.label: Laxative before niclosamide
nodes.rationale: Purges bowel of dead segments and enhances digestion and liberation of ova

nodes.label: Alpha-2 receptors
nodes.rationale: Presynaptic inhibitory autoreceptors/heteroreceptors; act by inhibiting adenylyl cyclase and lowering cAMP, so further norepinephrine release is inhibited.

nodes.label: Clonidine
nodes.rationale: Abrupt discontinuation must be avoided to prevent rebound hypertension; fluid retention on chronic therapy needs a diuretic. | Does not decrease renal blood flow or GFR, so useful in hypertension with renal disease.

nodes.label: Epinephrine reversal
nodes.rationale: Alpha-blockers abolish epinephrine vasoconstriction but not beta-2 vasodilation, so blood pressure falls; norepinephrine diminished not reversed; isoproterenol unaffected.

nodes.label: Methyldopa
nodes.rationale: Mainly used in pregnancy hypertension where it has a safety record; otherwise limited by adverse effects and multiple daily dosing.

nodes.label: Phenoxybenzamine
nodes.rationale: Irreversible, noncompetitive; block overcome only by new receptor synthesis, so action lasts about 24 hours. No longer used for hypertension (blocked presynaptic alpha-2 raises norepinephrine release, arrhythmias and angina).

nodes.label: Phentolamine
nodes.rationale: Competitive block of alpha-1 and alpha-2; effects last about 4 hours.

nodes.label: Rebound hypertension
nodes.rationale: Abrupt withdrawal of clonidine increases sympathetic activity; wean slowly.

nodes.label: Lisdexamfetamine
nodes.rationale: Only controlled (Schedule II) agent among the listed ADHD drugs.

nodes.label: Methylphenidate
nodes.rationale: Transdermal patch is for once-daily use, avoiding mid-day dosing.

nodes.label: Timolol
nodes.rationale: Decreases aqueous humor secretion by the ciliary body; does not change pupil size or near focus.

nodes.label: Figure 15.7 Adverse effects of amphetamines and methylphenidate
nodes.norm_label: figure 15.7 adverse effects of amphetamines and methylphenidate

nodes.label: Ion trapping in parasite food vacuole
nodes.norm_label: ion trapping in parasite food vacuole

nodes.label: Inhibition of leukotriene and prostaglandin synthesis
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of leukotriene and prostaglandin synthesis

nodes.label: Blocking autoinhibitory feedback of melanocortin system
nodes.norm_label: blocking autoinhibitory feedback of melanocortin system

nodes.label: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors
nodes.rationale: Not combined with GLP-1 receptor agonists (overlapping mechanisms and toxicity); unlike GLP-1 agonists they do not cause satiety and are weight neutral.

nodes.label: GLP-1 receptor agonists
nodes.rationale: Improve glucose-dependent insulin secretion, slow gastric emptying, enhance satiety, decrease postprandial glucagon, promote beta-cell proliferation; weight loss may occur.

nodes.label: HbA1c
nodes.rationale: Goal usually below 7% but individualized; a higher HbA1c is more likely to need insulin.

nodes.label: Incretin effect
nodes.rationale: Oral glucose gives more insulin secretion than equal IV glucose; markedly reduced in type 2 diabetes; incretins account for 60-70% of postprandial insulin secretion.

nodes.label: Linagliptin
nodes.rationale: Only DPP-4 inhibitor not needing dose adjustment in renal dysfunction (eliminated enterohepatically).

nodes.label: Fentanyl
nodes.rationale: Opioids are needed with inhalation agents because the latter alter consciousness but not pain perception.

nodes.label: Renal impairment
nodes.rationale: Saline sodium loading or liposomal products reduce nephrotoxicity; worsened by aminoglycosides, cyclosporine, vancomycin.

nodes.label: Dobutamine
nodes.rationale: Raises cardiac output without elevating myocardial oxygen demand as much as other sympathomimetics; caution in atrial fibrillation because it increases AV conduction.

nodes.label: Hypotension
nodes.rationale: Particularly in the elderly or those on diuretics; assess volume status before starting.

nodes.label: Inhibition of If current in SA node
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of if current in sa node

nodes.label: Class I, II, III and IV actions with alpha blockade
nodes.norm_label: class i, ii, iii and iv actions with alpha blockade

nodes.label: Binding parasite beta-tubulin inhibiting microtubule polymerization
nodes.norm_label: binding parasite beta-tubulin inhibiting microtubule polymerization

nodes.label: Flucytosine
nodes.rationale: Not used alone because resistant cells emerge rapidly; used with a second antifungal.

nodes.label: Folate synthesis and reduction inhibitor combination
nodes.norm_label: folate synthesis and reduction inhibitor combination

nodes.label: Griseofulvin
nodes.rationale: Replaced largely by terbinafine for onychomycosis; takes 6-12 months; absorption enhanced by high-fat meals.

nodes.label: Tinea capitis
nodes.rationale: Needs oral therapy; topical antifungals are ineffective.

nodes.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
nodes.rationale: WBCs view the synovium as non-self; T cells activate macrophages that release TNF-alpha and IL-1, causing joint destruction.

nodes.label: Atypical antipsychotics as adjuncts in depression
nodes.norm_label: atypical antipsychotics as adjuncts in depression

nodes.label: Bupropion
nodes.rationale: Avoid in patients at risk for seizures or with eating disorders such as bulimia.

nodes.label: Serotonin syndrome
nodes.rationale: Hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, sweating, myoclonus, altered mental status; risk highest with an MAOI or other highly serotonergic drug.

nodes.label: Biogenic amine theory
nodes.rationale: Overly simplistic: cannot explain why therapeutic response takes weeks while reuptake block is immediate.

nodes.label: Fludarabine
nodes.rationale: Given IV rather than orally because intestinal bacteria split off the sugar to yield very toxic fluoroadenine.

nodes.label: Immunosuppression
nodes.rationale: Rising mycoses are attributed to organ transplantation, cancer chemotherapy and HIV infection.

nodes.label: Alkylating agents
nodes.rationale: Do not discriminate between cycling and resting cells, though most toxic to rapidly dividing cells; all are mutagenic and carcinogenic.

nodes.label: Covalent binding to nucleophilic groups of DNA
nodes.norm_label: covalent binding to nucleophilic groups of dna

nodes.label: Nitrosoureas
nodes.rationale: Lipophilic so they penetrate the CNS, hence used for brain tumors.

nodes.label: Amphotericin B
nodes.rationale: Low therapeutic index; still drug of choice for several life-threatening mycoses.

nodes.label: Dermatophytes
nodes.rationale: Trichophyton, Microsporum and Epidermophyton cause most cutaneous infections (tinea).

nodes.label: Fever and chills
nodes.rationale: Premedicate with corticosteroid or antipyretic.

nodes.label: Liposomal amphotericin B
nodes.rationale: Reduced renal and infusion toxicity but more costly.

nodes.label: Thrombophlebitis
nodes.rationale: Adding heparin to the infusion alleviates it.

nodes.label: Bacterial resistance
nodes.rationale: Limited by using antibiotics with other acne agents, shortest oral course, low-dose dosing, and nonantibiotic maintenance after clearing.

nodes.label: Inhibition of RNA polymerase sigma subunit
nodes.norm_label: inhibition of rna polymerase sigma subunit

nodes.label: Quinupristin/dalfopristin
nodes.rationale: Not effective

nodes.label: Carbamazepine
nodes.rationale: Introduced at low dose (100 to 200 mg daily) so tolerance to CNS side effects develops; strong enzyme inducer, so it lowers levels of oral contraceptives, valproate, anticoagulants and others. | May make absence seizures more frequent.

nodes.label: Enzyme induction by antiseizure drugs
nodes.rationale: These drugs increase contraceptive metabolism with any delivery system, so the contraceptive may fail.

nodes.label: Therapeutic index
nodes.rationale: TI = TD50/ED50; larger value means a wider safety margin. Low-TI drugs are still used in serious disease when risk of leaving it untreated outweighs adverse effects. | TI = TD50/ED50; a low TI means dose is critical and altered bioavailability changes therapeutic and adverse effects (warfarin).

nodes.label: Free radical production from endoperoxide bridge cleavage
nodes.norm_label: free radical production from endoperoxide bridge cleavage

nodes.label: Reductive scission of peroxide bridge by heme-iron
nodes.norm_label: reductive scission of peroxide bridge by heme-iron

nodes.label: Glimepiride
nodes.rationale: Safer than glybenclamide in renal dysfunction and the elderly.

nodes.label: Glinides
nodes.rationale: Rapid onset, short duration; effective for early post-meal insulin release (postprandial glucose regulators); not combined with sulfonylureas because of overlapping mechanism and serious hypoglycemia.

nodes.label: Glipizide
nodes.rationale: Safer than glybenclamide in renal dysfunction and the elderly.

nodes.label: Hypoglycemia
nodes.rationale: Most serious and common insulin adverse effect; symptoms include tachycardia, confusion, sweating, shakiness, blurred vision.

nodes.label: Intensive insulin therapy
nodes.rationale: Three or more injections daily with frequent glucose monitoring; not recommended in long-standing diabetes, significant microvascular complications, advanced age, or hypoglycemic unawareness because of hypoglycemia risk.

nodes.label: Standard insulin therapy
nodes.rationale: Twice-daily injections.

nodes.label: Sulfonylureas
nodes.rationale: Block ATP-sensitive K+ channels causing depolarization, Ca2+ influx and insulin exocytosis; may also reduce hepatic glucose production and increase peripheral insulin sensitivity.

nodes.label: Mixed opioid agonist-antagonists and partial agonists
nodes.norm_label: mixed opioid agonist-antagonists and partial agonists

nodes.label: Hemorrhagic cystitis
nodes.rationale: Acrolein, a cyclophosphamide metabolite, accumulates in the bladder.

nodes.label: Mesna
nodes.rationale: Neutralizes toxic metabolites in the urine; given with hydration. | Neutralizes the toxic metabolites of ifosfamide; allopurinol and leucovorin do not prevent hemorrhagic cystitis.

nodes.label: Competitive blockade of histamine H2 receptors
nodes.norm_label: competitive blockade of histamine h2 receptors

nodes.label: Cell cycle-specific drugs
nodes.rationale: Effective only against replicating (dividing) cells; nondividing G0 cells usually survive.

nodes.label: Hepatic CYP450 metabolism and biliary excretion
nodes.norm_label: hepatic cyp450 metabolism and biliary excretion

nodes.label: Paclitaxel
nodes.rationale: Premedicate with dexamethasone, diphenhydramine and an H2 blocker because of serious hypersensitivity reactions.

nodes.label: Vinca alkaloids
nodes.rationale: Must not be given intrathecally; this error can cause death.

nodes.label: Log kill
nodes.rationale: Drug kills a constant fraction of cells (first-order); a 5-log kill leaves about 10^4 of 10^9 cells, and tumor cells (unlike bacteria) need further treatment to eradicate.
